newsitem.title: UK: Thames sees small cut in profit from new tax.
newsitem.headline: Thames sees small cut in profit from new tax.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Thames Water Plc expects a small decrease in profits as a result of a one-off tax on excess profits imposed by the new Labour government, chief financial officer David Luffrum said on Wednesday.
"There will be a small reduction in profits of the company as a result of the windfall tax," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

Luffrum said the amount would be "fairly modest," adding that increased interest payments on borrowings to pay for the so called "windfall" tax should impact by around three to four million stg this year.
He said the impact in a full year after payment of all the tax, which will amount to 230 million stg for Thames, would be 15-20 million stg.
Luffrum added that borrowings to cover the windfall tax payment would increase gearing by around eight percent in two years.
The Labour government introduced the tax, aimed at raising 5.2 billion stg, in its first budget on July 2.
